controls.name: Random example selection baseline (ICL)
controls.detail: Use size-matched random few-shot example sets from the allowed pool.
controls.rules_out: That improvements are due to adding examples at all rather than the proposed selection/organization strategy.

controls.name: Oracle/upper-bound selection
controls.detail: Use ground-truth target (e.g., gold SQL) to select examples/demonstrations.
controls.rules_out: Ceiling attributable to perfect selection, isolating selection algorithm limitations from inherent task limits.
evidence: Text-to-SQL Empowered by Large Language Models: A Benchmark Evaluation

controls.name: Vanilla no-retrieval baseline
controls.detail: Generate code without any external retrieval/augmentation.
controls.rules_out: That gains are from the base LLM rather than the retrieval/evolution intervention.
evidence: EVOR: Evolving Retrieval for Code Generation

controls.name: BM25 retrieval baseline
controls.detail: Apply keyword-based BM25 on the same corpus.
controls.rules_out: That improvements stem from generic keyword search rather than the proposed dense/learned or structured retrieval.

controls.name: Documentation-only retrieval (DocPrompting)
controls.detail: Retrieve only static documentation as context for generation.
controls.rules_out: That using any retrieved text (docs alone) explains gains rather than the full evolved/retrieval design.
evidence: EVOR: Evolving Retrieval for Code Generation

controls.name: Knowledge evidence ablation (w/knowledge vs w/o knowledge)
controls.detail: Evaluate with and without externally provided ground-truth evidence.
controls.rules_out: That performance changes are due to unrelated prompt differences instead of external knowledge provision.
evidence: Can LLM Already Serve as A Database Interface? A BIg Bench for Large-Scale Database Grounded Text-to-SQLs

controls.name: Backbone substitution / size-matched baselines
controls.detail: Run the same method across multiple backbone LMs (sizes/families) or compare against base vs instruction-tuned variants.

controls.name: w/REF vs w/oREF for LLM evaluators

controls.name: Deterministic vs sampling regime

controls.name: Schema normalization control

controls.name: Train–test description alignment

controls.name: Alternative DBMS and rule-based reference rewrites

controls.name: Structure/metadata ablations

controls.name: Human performance reference
controls.detail: Measure expert human performance on the same split.

evidence: Can LLM Already Serve as A Database Interface? A BIg Bench for Large-Scale Database Grounded Text-to-SQLs

controls.name: Efficiency equivalence control
controls.detail: Compare original vs semantically equivalent optimized queries.
controls.rules_out: That efficiency gains arise from semantic changes or incorrect results.
evidence: Can LLM Already Serve as A Database Interface? A BIg Bench for Large-Scale Database Grounded Text-to-SQLs

controls.name: No-retrieval memorization check
controls.detail: Probe base LLMs without any retrieval/context for target-specific knowledge.
controls.rules_out: That high performance is due to pretraining memorization rather than retrieval.
evidence: DeepCodeSeek: Real-Time API Retrieval for Context-Aware Code Generation

controls.name: Out-of-distribution test set
controls.detail: Evaluate on a held-out OOD split not seen in any training/synthetic data.
controls.rules_out: That improvements are due to overfitting or catastrophic forgetting.

confounds.name: Training data contamination / benchmark leakage
confounds.detail: Benchmark items (or near-duplicates) may be in pretraining/fine-tuning data, inflating scores.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Deduplicate and decontaminate benchmarks; document procedures or use continuously updated sources.
evidence: Benchmarks and Metrics for Evaluations of Code Generation: A Critical Review
DOMAINEVAL: An Auto-Constructed Benchmark for Multi-Domain Code Generation

confounds.name: Surface similarity does not imply functional correctness
confounds.detail: High BLEU/ROUGE/Code similarity may not reflect executable correctness.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Prioritize execution-based metrics (pass@k/TPR) and/or human judgments; report weak correlations of text metrics to functionality.
evidence: A Survey on Evaluating Large Language Models in Code Generation Tasks
Benchmarks and Metrics for Evaluations of Code Generation: A Critical Review

confounds.name: Insufficient test-suite adequacy
confounds.detail: Weak tests miss incorrect behaviors, overestimating correctness.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Report and aim for high branch/statement coverage; use benchmarks with strong coverage; acknowledge residual gaps.
evidence: Benchmarks and Metrics for Evaluations of Code Generation: A Critical Review

confounds.name: Single-reference SQL and tie-handling artifacts
confounds.detail: Correct SQL may fail metrics due to LIMIT/ORDER BY ties or GROUP BY formulation.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Apply deterministic rewrites (tie-preserving LIMIT, GROUP BY fixes) and recompute metrics.
evidence: Evaluating Cross-Domain Text-to-SQL Models and Benchmarks

confounds.name: Schema-mapping ambiguity in Text-to-SQL
confounds.detail: Multiple valid schema mappings exist but benchmarks provide a single reference.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Expert human evaluation with schema inspection and adjudication.
evidence: Evaluating Cross-Domain Text-to-SQL Models and Benchmarks

confounds.name: Wrong database content assumptions
confounds.detail: Ground-truth queries rely on assumptions not supported by DB contents.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Manual DB validation during annotation/human eval and correction of mislabeled items.
evidence: Evaluating Cross-Domain Text-to-SQL Models and Benchmarks

confounds.name: Randomness in decoding
confounds.detail: Stochastic sampling yields variable outcomes mistaken as method gains.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Use temperature=0 for deterministic comparisons or average across multiple repeated runs/seeds.
evidence: CodeJudge: Evaluating Code Generation with Large Language Models
Text-to-SQL Empowered by Large Language Models: A Benchmark Evaluation

confounds.name: Pass@k undercounts partial correctness
confounds.detail: Programs that pass many tests but not all are scored as failures.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Also report fractional test pass metrics (AvgPassRatio/TPR).
evidence: AixBench: A Code Generation Benchmark Dataset

confounds.name: Efficiency inflated by incorrect results
confounds.detail: Faster but wrong outputs bias efficiency metrics.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Gate efficiency by correctness (e.g., VES counts only valid outputs).

confounds.name: Pretraining memorization explains retrieval gains

confounds.ruled_out_by: No-retrieval probes showing low accuracy; then add retrieval for comparison.

confounds.name: Evaluator relies on seeing the reference
confounds.detail: LLM-based evaluators may key off the gold solution rather than reason about correctness.

confounds.name: Gains due to evaluator model size/vendor

confounds.name: Dataset difficulty or prompt mismatch drives gaps

confounds.name: Catastrophic forgetting after specialization
confounds.detail: Domain fine-tuning harms general code abilities, masking trade-offs.

evidence: DeepCodeSeek: Real-Time API Retrieval for Context-Aware Code Generation

confounds.name: Missing imports/dependencies cause execution failures
confounds.detail: Test failures reflect missing context rather than generation quality.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Auto-include required context/imports and trace dependencies before execution.
evidence: DOMAINEVAL: An Auto-Constructed Benchmark for Multi-Domain Code Generation

confounds.name: Unsafe code skews evaluation or must be discarded
confounds.detail: Dangerous operations bias results or force filtering.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Execute in sandbox and filter via banned-keyword lists; report safety filtering.
evidence: DOMAINEVAL: An Auto-Constructed Benchmark for Multi-Domain Code Generation

confounds.name: Multi-trial pass@k overstates interactive usability
confounds.detail: Independent sampling differs from sequential user attempts.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Also report interactive/user-centric metrics (e.g., #attempts, time-to-completion, usability Likerts).
evidence: Benchmarks and Metrics for Evaluations of Code Generation: A Critical Review

confounds.name: Human evaluation bias from model identity
confounds.detail: Knowing model identities biases subjective ratings.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Blind peer review and multi-round comparative judging.
evidence: A Survey on Evaluating Large Language Models in Code Generation Tasks

confounds.name: Runtime measurement noise
confounds.detail: System variability inflates/obscures efficiency differences.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Repeated runs on fixed hardware with outlier removal and averaging.
evidence: Can LLM Already Serve as A Database Interface? A BIg Bench for Large-Scale Database Grounded Text-to-SQLs

confounds.name: Prompt-length/token-count explains gains
confounds.detail: Improvements arise from longer prompts (e.g., added schema/keys) rather than the method.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Length-matched ablations removing specific structural hints or phrasing and re-evaluating.

confounds.name: Example surface similarity drives ICL gains
confounds.detail: Selected demos are trivially similar to targets, not due to selection quality.

confounds.name: API invocation vs implementation ability
confounds.detail: Tasks are solved by calling APIs rather than implementing logic.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Use benchmarks built from implementation functions with tests focusing on concrete functionality.

confounds.name: Overfitting to small synthetic training data
confounds.detail: Synthetic RL datasets cause narrow gains that don't generalize.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Start from broader SFT checkpoints, limit synthetic fine-tuning, monitor learning curves, and validate on OOD sets.

KaggleDBQA: Realistic Evaluation of Text-to-SQL Parsers

Evaluating Cross-Domain Text-to-SQL Models and Benchmarks
protocols.detail: Use at least two independent expert annotators with reconciliation for SQL correctness; or ≥3 annotators with majority vote and Likert grammar scores for NL responses.

protocols.name: Latency and token-budget reporting
evidence: DeepCodeSeek: Real-Time API Retrieval for Context-Aware Code Generation
EVOR: Evolving Retrieval for Code Generation

protocols.name: Zero-shot and few-shot ICL settings
evidence: Can LLM Already Serve as A Database Interface? A BIg Bench for Large-Scale Database Grounded Text-to-SQLs
Text-to-SQL Empowered by Large Language Models: A Benchmark Evaluation
protocols.detail: Evaluate in both zero-shot and few-shot modes; draw examples from training pools disjoint in schema from evaluation databases.

protocols.name: Alternative DBMS validation and reference rewrites
evidence: Evaluating Cross-Domain Text-to-SQL Models and Benchmarks
protocols.detail: Migrate datasets to a stricter DBMS (e.g., PostgreSQL) and apply deterministic rewrites (e.g., tie-preserving LIMIT, GROUP BY fixes) to reassess metric failures.

protocols.name: Database-split for cross-domain Text-to-SQL
evidence: CoSQL: A Conversational Text-to-SQL Challenge Towards Cross-Domain Natural Language Interfaces to Databases
protocols.detail: Split train/dev/test by database to ensure evaluation on unseen schemas and prevent DB memorization.

protocols.name: Dataset hygiene
evidence: Benchmarks and Metrics for Evaluations of Code Generation: A Critical Review
protocols.detail: Apply deduplication and decontamination against model training data; document procedures.

protocols.name: Deterministic pass@1 and sampled pass@k
evidence: DOMAINEVAL: An Auto-Constructed Benchmark for Multi-Domain Code Generation
protocols.detail: Report Pass@1 with greedy decoding (temperature=0); report Pass@k with stochastic sampling (e.g., temperature≈0.2, top-p≈0.95) with sufficient samples.

protocols.name: Dialogue protocols for conversational SQL
evidence: CoSQL: A Conversational Text-to-SQL Challenge Towards Cross-Domain Natural Language Interfaces to Databases
protocols.detail: For DST tasks, forbid access to gold previous-turn SQL and evaluate with Question/Interaction-level exact match; report BLEU and human logic/grammar on responses.

protocols.name: Efficiency measurement robustness
evidence: Can LLM Already Serve as A Database Interface? A BIg Bench for Large-Scale Database Grounded Text-to-SQLs
protocols.detail: Measure SQL/query runtime by running each query many times (e.g., 100x) on the same hardware, drop outliers, and average.

protocols.name: Macro-averaging across domains
evidence: DOMAINEVAL: An Auto-Constructed Benchmark for Multi-Domain Code Generation
protocols.detail: For multi-domain code benchmarks, report macro-average and standard deviation across domains.

protocols.name: Out-of-distribution evaluation
evidence: DeepCodeSeek: Real-Time API Retrieval for Context-Aware Code Generation
protocols.detail: Assess generalization on a held-out OOD set not used in any training/fine-tuning.

controls.name: Backbone substitution / size-matched baselines
evidence: CodeJudge: Evaluating Code Generation with Large Language Models
DOMAINEVAL: An Auto-Constructed Benchmark for Multi-Domain Code Generation
LGESQL: Line Graph Enhanced Text-to-SQL Model with Mixed Local and Non-Local Relations
controls.detail: Run the same method across multiple backbone LMs (sizes/families) or compare against base vs instruction-tuned variants.
controls.rules_out: That gains come from a particular large/proprietary model or instruction tuning rather than the method.

controls.name: BM25 retrieval baseline
evidence: DeepCodeSeek: Real-Time API Retrieval for Context-Aware Code Generation
EVOR: Evolving Retrieval for Code Generation
controls.detail: Generate code without any external retrieval/augmentation.
controls.rules_out: That improvements stem from generic keyword search rather than the proposed dense/learned or structured retrieval.

controls.name: Alternative DBMS and rule-based reference rewrites
evidence: Evaluating Cross-Domain Text-to-SQL Models and Benchmarks
controls.detail: Re-evaluate after migrating to a stricter DBMS and applying deterministic rewrites (e.g., tie-handling, GROUP BY).
controls.rules_out: That metric failures stem from permissive SQL dialects or reference-query artifacts.

controls.name: Deterministic vs sampling regime
evidence: DOMAINEVAL: An Auto-Constructed Benchmark for Multi-Domain Code Generation
controls.detail: Compare greedy N=1 decoding to multi-sample stochastic decoding at fixed settings.
controls.rules_out: That observed gains are purely a byproduct of sampling more candidates rather than the method.

controls.name: Documentation-only retrieval
evidence: EVOR: Evolving Retrieval for Code Generation
controls.detail: Retrieve only static documentation as context for generation.
controls.rules_out: That using any retrieved text (docs alone) explains gains rather than the full evolved/retrieval design.

controls.name: Efficiency equivalence control
evidence: Can LLM Already Serve as A Database Interface? A BIg Bench for Large-Scale Database Grounded Text-to-SQLs
controls.detail: Compare original vs semantically equivalent optimized queries.
controls.rules_out: That efficiency gains arise from semantic changes or incorrect results.

controls.name: Human performance reference
evidence: Can LLM Already Serve as A Database Interface? A BIg Bench for Large-Scale Database Grounded Text-to-SQLs
controls.detail: Measure expert human performance on the same split.
controls.rules_out: That models have already matched practical human-level performance; sets an empirical upper bound.

controls.name: Knowledge evidence ablation
evidence: Can LLM Already Serve as A Database Interface? A BIg Bench for Large-Scale Database Grounded Text-to-SQLs
variants: Knowledge evidence ablation (w/knowledge vs w/o knowledge)
controls.detail: Evaluate with and without externally provided ground-truth evidence.
controls.rules_out: That performance changes are due to unrelated prompt differences instead of external knowledge provision.

controls.name: No-retrieval memorization check
evidence: DeepCodeSeek: Real-Time API Retrieval for Context-Aware Code Generation
controls.detail: Probe base LLMs without any retrieval/context for target-specific knowledge.
controls.rules_out: That high performance is due to pretraining memorization rather than retrieval.

controls.name: Oracle/upper-bound selection
evidence: Text-to-SQL Empowered by Large Language Models: A Benchmark Evaluation
controls.detail: Use ground-truth target (e.g., gold SQL) to select examples/demonstrations.
controls.rules_out: Ceiling attributable to perfect selection, isolating selection algorithm limitations from inherent task limits.

controls.name: Out-of-distribution test set
evidence: DeepCodeSeek: Real-Time API Retrieval for Context-Aware Code Generation
controls.detail: Evaluate on a held-out OOD split not seen in any training/synthetic data.
controls.rules_out: That improvements are due to overfitting or catastrophic forgetting.

controls.name: Random example selection baseline
evidence: Text-to-SQL Empowered by Large Language Models: A Benchmark Evaluation
controls.detail: Use size-matched random few-shot example sets from the allowed pool.
controls.rules_out: That improvements are due to adding examples at all rather than the proposed selection/organization strategy.

controls.name: Schema normalization control
evidence: KaggleDBQA: Realistic Evaluation of Text-to-SQL Parsers
controls.detail: Evaluate with manually normalized/expanded schema names without adding extra knowledge.
controls.rules_out: That benefits attributed to documentation arise from simple name clarifications.

controls.name: Structure/metadata ablations
evidence: Text-to-SQL Empowered by Large Language Models: A Benchmark Evaluation
controls.detail: Remove/alter specific structural hints (e.g., foreign keys, schema info) or enforce length-matched prompts.
controls.rules_out: That gains are driven by additional tokens/length or a specific phrasing rather than the proposed representation.

confounds.name: Dataset difficulty or prompt mismatch drives gaps
evidence: Can LLM Already Serve as A Database Interface? A BIg Bench for Large-Scale Database Grounded Text-to-SQLs
KaggleDBQA: Realistic Evaluation of Text-to-SQL Parsers
confounds.detail: Performance differences stem from dataset hardness or prompt/knowledge disparities.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Use identical prompts and knowledge across datasets; report dataset statistics (e.g., SQL hardness, mention rates).

confounds.name: Pass@k undercounts partial correctness
evidence: AixBench: A Code Generation Benchmark Dataset
Benchmarks and Metrics for Evaluations of Code Generation: A Critical Review
confounds.detail: Programs that pass many tests but not all are scored as failures.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Also report fractional test pass metrics (AvgPassRatio/TPR).

confounds.name: Randomness in decoding
evidence: CodeJudge: Evaluating Code Generation with Large Language Models
Text-to-SQL Empowered by Large Language Models: A Benchmark Evaluation
confounds.detail: Stochastic sampling yields variable outcomes mistaken as method gains.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Use temperature=0 for deterministic comparisons or average across multiple repeated runs/seeds.

confounds.name: Surface similarity does not imply functional correctness
evidence: A Survey on Evaluating Large Language Models in Code Generation Tasks
Benchmarks and Metrics for Evaluations of Code Generation: A Critical Review
confounds.detail: High BLEU/ROUGE/Code similarity may not reflect executable correctness.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Prioritize execution-based metrics (pass@k/TPR) and/or human judgments; report weak correlations of text metrics to functionality.

confounds.name: Training data contamination / benchmark leakage
evidence: Benchmarks and Metrics for Evaluations of Code Generation: A Critical Review
DOMAINEVAL: An Auto-Constructed Benchmark for Multi-Domain Code Generation
confounds.detail: Benchmark items (or near-duplicates) may be in pretraining/fine-tuning data, inflating scores.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Deduplicate and decontaminate benchmarks; document procedures or use continuously updated sources.

confounds.name: API invocation vs implementation ability
evidence: DOMAINEVAL: An Auto-Constructed Benchmark for Multi-Domain Code Generation
confounds.detail: Tasks are solved by calling APIs rather than implementing logic.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Use benchmarks built from implementation functions with tests focusing on concrete functionality.

confounds.name: Catastrophic forgetting after specialization
evidence: DeepCodeSeek: Real-Time API Retrieval for Context-Aware Code Generation
confounds.detail: Domain fine-tuning harms general code abilities, masking trade-offs.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Evaluate on OOD sets and compare to base model.

confounds.name: Efficiency inflated by incorrect results
evidence: Can LLM Already Serve as A Database Interface? A BIg Bench for Large-Scale Database Grounded Text-to-SQLs
confounds.detail: Faster but wrong outputs bias efficiency metrics.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Gate efficiency by correctness (e.g., VES counts only valid outputs).

confounds.name: Evaluator relies on seeing the reference
evidence: CodeJudge: Evaluating Code Generation with Large Language Models
confounds.detail: LLM-based evaluators may key off the gold solution rather than reason about correctness.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Evaluate w/REF and w/oREF; maintain performance without reference access.

confounds.name: Example surface similarity drives ICL gains
evidence: Text-to-SQL Empowered by Large Language Models: A Benchmark Evaluation
confounds.detail: Selected demos are trivially similar to targets, not due to selection quality.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Quantify similarity (e.g., Jaccard) vs accuracy and compare to oracle/upper bounds.

confounds.name: Gains due to evaluator model size/vendor
evidence: CodeJudge: Evaluating Code Generation with Large Language Models
confounds.detail: Results hinge on a specific large/proprietary evaluator.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Replicate with multiple evaluator LMs of varying sizes (including open-source) and compare correlations/accuracy.

confounds.name: Human evaluation bias from model identity
evidence: A Survey on Evaluating Large Language Models in Code Generation Tasks
confounds.detail: Knowing model identities biases subjective ratings.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Blind peer review and multi-round comparative judging.

confounds.name: Insufficient test-suite adequacy
evidence: Benchmarks and Metrics for Evaluations of Code Generation: A Critical Review
confounds.detail: Weak tests miss incorrect behaviors, overestimating correctness.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Report and aim for high branch/statement coverage; use benchmarks with strong coverage; acknowledge residual gaps.

confounds.name: Missing imports/dependencies cause execution failures
evidence: DOMAINEVAL: An Auto-Constructed Benchmark for Multi-Domain Code Generation
confounds.detail: Test failures reflect missing context rather than generation quality.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Auto-include required context/imports and trace dependencies before execution.

experiment_recipes.pass_condition: Run the full HumanEval Pass@1 evaluation three times with temperature=0 (greedy). Success if (a) the generated code is byte-identical across all three runs for ≥99% of problems and (b) Pass@1 is exactly identical across runs (variance=0). Otherwise refute determinism compliance.
experiment_recipes.rationale: Verifies the environment truly produces deterministic outputs for Pass@1 as required by standard practice before any stochastic sampling comparisons.

experiment_recipes.goal: Sandboxed execution and safety filters validated
experiment_recipes.attack_or_condition: Sandboxed code execution with safety filters
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: Using a banned-keyword filter (e.g., os.system, subprocess, socket, shutil.rmtree, requests, open with write/append), run ≥20 curated unsafe snippets: Compilation/Interpretation success rate must be 0%. On HumanEval unit tests with auto-imports/context enabled, Compilation/Interpretation success rate must be ≥95%. Both conditions must hold to pass.
experiment_recipes.rationale: Confirms the execution harness blocks dangerous operations while still reliably executing benign code, a prerequisite for valid execution-based evaluation.

experiment_recipes.goal: Spider official evaluation harness correctness established
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: Feed the gold SQL as the model outputs over the Spider dev set. Success if EX=100% and EM=100%. Additionally, when appending a dummy trailing statement to the gold output (e.g., '; SELECT 1'), EX and EM must remain unchanged (0.0 pp difference), confirming first-SQL extraction is enforced.
constraints_not_enforced: Database-split for cross-domain Text-to-SQL (no training performed)
experiment_recipes.rationale: Validates the use of the official Spider evaluator and the first-SQL extraction rule before testing any model.

experiment_recipes.attack_or_condition: Execution-based functional evaluation with unit tests — Compile (when applicable) and execute generated code on benchmark-provided tests; report pass@k and/or test pass rates; use unbiased pass@k estimator when sampling many outputs.
experiment_recipes.pass_condition:
- Deterministic Pass@1: evaluate with temperature=0 (greedy).
- Sampled Pass@10: temperature=0.2, top-p=0.95, and ≥200 samples per problem; compute the unbiased Pass@10 estimator.
- Multiple seeds: repeat the entire stochastic evaluation for ≥3 random seeds and report mean and standard error.
- Sanity: unbiased Pass@10 ≥ Pass@1 + 1.0 percentage points.
- Harness health: overall Compilation/Interpretation success rate across all generated samples ≥85%.
All five conditions must be met to pass.
depends_on: Sandboxed execution and safety filters validated
experiment_recipes.rationale: Enforces core norms: deterministic Pass@1, sufficiently sampled unbiased Pass@k with multiple seeds and error bars, and execution-based functional metrics.

experiment_recipes.pass_condition:
- Use the official Spider test-suite-sql-eval; evaluate on the dev split only with unseen databases.
- Enforce first-SQL extraction (validated in the apparatus recipe); predictions containing multiple SQLs must be evaluated only on the first SQL.
- Report both EX and EM.
- If stochastic decoding is used: run ≥3 seeds and report mean and standard error; otherwise use temperature=0.
All listed conditions must be satisfied to pass.
constraints_not_enforced: Database-split for cross-domain Text-to-SQL (no training performed)
Alternative DBMS validation and reference rewrites
depends_on: Spider official evaluation harness correctness established
experiment_recipes.rationale: Checks that Spider evaluation follows the official, execution-centered norms and reporting requirements with seed control.

experiment_recipes.goal: Budget-matched baselines and decoding controls for code-gen
experiment_recipes.pass_condition: Run three matched conditions on BigCodeBench: (1) Vanilla no-retrieval baseline with greedy Pass@1; (2) Same baseline with sampled Pass@10 using ≥200 samples/problem; (3) EVOR with sampled Pass@10 using ≥200 samples/problem. Success if: (a) average prompt+generation tokens per attempt across all three conditions differ by ≤5% (matched budgets), (b) sample counts per problem are identical across (2) and (3), and (c) the baseline sampled Pass@10 ≥ baseline Pass@1 + 1.0 percentage points (verifies correct sampling benefit). All must hold to pass.
depends_on: Sandboxed execution and safety filters validated
experiment_recipes.rationale: Attributes gains to the intended mechanism rather than sampling or budget artifacts by enforcing matched budgets and decoding controls, and reporting execution-based metrics including AvgPassRatio.
